ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a parallelogram, with the base labeled 12 yd. On the left side there is a pink dashed vertical height, extending downward from the upper-left vertex to the horizontal line where the base lies; the horizontal distance from the bottom of the dashed line to the lower-left vertex of the parallelogram is labeled 4 yd, and the angle between the dashed vertical height and the left slanted side is labeled 35°. Reasoning: Treat the left dashed-line part as a right triangle, and let the height of the parallelogram be h. In this right triangle, the opposite side of the 35° angle is 4 yd, and the adjacent side is h, so tan(35°)=4/h. Solving gives h=4/tan(35°). The parallelogram area A=base×height=12·h=12·(4/tan(35°))≈68.55 square yards, according to the commonly used answer for the problem, it is about 68.6.

The dashed vertical foot is 4 yd left of the lower-left vertex, so it is at (-4,0), and the upper-left vertex is at (-4,h).
